question: Can a nearest-neighbor retrieval over cached decoder representations, added to a pre-trained MT model with no training, improve translation in-domain, out-of-domain and multilingually?
hypothesis: Translation contexts that are close in the MT model's representation space are more likely to be followed by the same target word.
contributions: kNN-MT: interpolates the MT softmax with a kNN distribution over a datastore of (decoder representation, target token) pairs, no extra training
Gains of 1.5 BLEU on a SOTA de-en model, 9.2 BLEU average domain-adaptation gain, and up to 3 BLEU for a multilingual model specialised per language pair
Qualitative analysis showing retrievals combine source and target context

method.summary: A FAISS datastore is built offline from one forward pass of a trained MT model over parallel data; keys are the 1024-d decoder representation input to the final feedforward layer, values are the gold target token. At each decoding step the top-k neighbours by squared L2 give a softmax-with-temperature distribution over tokens, interpolated with the model distribution by lambda; decoding is beam search.
method.task: machine translation (single pair, multilingual, domain adaptation)

datasets.name: CCMatrix
datasets.split: datastores per language pair from its training pairs
datasets.source: Schwenk et al., 2019; pairs with distance measure >= 1.06

datasets.name: Multi-domains (Koehn & Knowles, 2017; re-split Aharoni & Goldberg, 2020)
datasets.size: in-domain datastore: Medical 5.70M, Law 18.3M, IT 3.10M, Koran 450K, Subtitles 159M
datasets.split: train datastore, 2,000 test sentences per domain

other.extra_training: over 10 billion tokens of backtranslation data; fine-tuned on newstest sets before 2018

other.training: 100K updates on CCMatrix, temperature upsampling T=5

inference.decoding: beam search, beam size 5 (Appendix A); beam 1 and lambda=1 for qualitative analysis
inference.retrieval: FAISS index, keys quantised to 64 bytes, clustered; k=64 neighbours, 32 clusters searched; squared-L2 distance; key = 1024-d representation input to final-layer FFN

parameters.clusters_trained: 131K clusters from 5M keys (multilingual); 4K clusters from 1M keys (domain adaptation in-domain)

other.cost: datastore build is one forward pass; generation about two orders of magnitude slower than base MT with billion-item datastore

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: case-sensitive detokenized SacreBLEU, signature BLEU+case.mixed+numrefs.1+smooth.exp+tok.13a+version.1.4.13 (tok.zh, tok.ja-mecab for zh, ja)

baselines: Aharoni & Goldberg (2020): per-domain models, all-domain model, best data selection
eval.protocol: Hyperparameters (lambda, T) tuned on validation sets; significance by power analysis of Card et al. (2020), bold in Table 1; about 2,000-example test sets with >=1 BLEU gains considered powered

limits: Inference is about two orders of magnitude slower than the base model with billion-scale datastores; authors name faster search as open work.
lambda and T tuned on validation per language pair or domain; k, clusters and beam fixed, k not tuned.
Multilingual datastores are built from data the model was trained on; in-domain datastore gains for the multi-domain set are over a base never trained on those domains.
Only translation evaluated; only BLEU, no human evaluation.
Authors say further investigation is needed on cross-lingual retrieval across related and unrelated languages.
No seeds or variance reported beyond a power analysis; no latency or memory numbers given.
Code stated as 'will be available', not confirmed.

terms.definition: augmenting the decoder of a pre-trained machine translation model with a nearest neighbor retrieval mechanism, allowing the model direct access to a datastore of cached examples

lineage.work: Generalization through memorization: Nearest neighbor language models (Khandelwal et al.)
lineage.note: kNN-MT generalises kNN-LM to conditional generation: keys include source context, plus a softmax temperature
lineage.quote: kNN-MT is a generalization of kNN-LM applied to conditional sequence generation

lineage.work: Billion-scale similarity search with GPUs (FAISS, Johnson et al.)
Facebook FAIR's WMT19 news translation submission (Ng et al.)
Unsupervised domain clusters in pretrained language models (Aharoni & Goldberg)
Search engine guided NMT (Gu et al.)

lineage.note: retrieval concatenated into inputs, versus kNN-MT interpolating output distributions

lineage.work: With little power comes great responsibility (Card et al.)

code.snippet: (K, V) = {(f(s, t_{1:i-1}), t_i), for all t_i in t | (s, t) in (S, T)}; p_kNN(y_i|x, y^_{1:i-1}) ∝ sum_{(k_j,v_j) in N} 1[y_i=v_j] exp(-d(k_j, f(x, y^_{1:i-1}))/T); p = λ p_kNN + (1-λ) p_MT
